entry.title: eMudhra intermediate CA compromise
entry.summary:
Mozilla has announced that it has received a report that private keys associated with eight eMudhra intermediate certificates have been compromised: These keys could allow attackers to issue fraudulent HTTPS certificates for websites they do not control. An attacker who could intercept a user's connection could use those certificates to impersonate websites and potentially read or modify traffic. Mozilla has blocked the affected certificates using its OneCRL centralized list of revoked certificates, and has updated the trusted certificate list in Network Security Services (NSS) 3.131.1 .

Source: Hacker News · Tags: #software-architecture #open-source

entry.title: Evolving Agent Interfaces. Computer-use agents are limited by the interfaces humans give them.
entry.summary:
Computer-use agents are limited by the interfaces humans give them. An agent may type a spreadsheet cell by cell when a single line of code would do, or print all two thousand lines of a file through a shell to find one function. Both the interfaces and the knowledge of when to use each are built by hand, which cannot keep pace with new applications, workflows, and models.

entry.title: Specter: Fast MoE Inference via Quantization-Enabled Multi-Step Speculative Offloading
entry.summary:
Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models often exceed a single accelerator's memory capacity. Offloading experts to host memory creates a severe PCIe I/O bottleneck because data-dependent routing keeps transfers on the critical path. We present Specter, an inference system that uses quantization to combine speculative decoding with expert offloading.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #inference

entry.title: Painting Change Map as guidance for generating painting processes
entry.summary:
Digital art generation has undergone a massive paradigm shift, moving from static image synthesis to dynamic video generation that can mimic the human painting process. While existing models can synthesize visually stunning time-lapses of paintings being created or "unpainted," they largely treat the creative process as a black box. Current conditioning mechanisms are either too rigid, relying on static geometric cues like Canny edges or depth maps, or too holistic, utilizing simple scalar progress variables that offer no localized control.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights

entry.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
entry.summary:
Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities. We study the persistent yet often overlooked brain--body mismatch problem in this paradigm, where an evolving harness (body) demands behaviors its model (brain) has not learned or restricts capabilities it already possesses. We introduce CoEvo-RSI, a RSI framework that advances model--harness co-evolution through agent-driven, bidirectional historical inheritance.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents

entry.title: Event-STVG: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding for Long-Form Event Reasoning. Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (STVG) aims to jointly localize a target in space and time given a natural-language query.
entry.summary:
Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (STVG) aims to jointly localize a target in space and time given a natural-language query. Despite continued advances, existing STVG benchmarks remain largely centered on localizing targets through instance-specific descriptions, leaving them largely decoupled from long-form reasoning increasingly emphasized in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). In this paper, we introduce Event-STVG, a task that shifts STVG from locating what is described toward event-level reasoning by unifying long-form context, repeated-event reasoning, event localization, role inference, and multi-target grounding.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #clean-tech

entry.title: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems. Decision models support routing, guardrails, and output verification in LLM systems.
entry.summary:
Decision models support routing, guardrails, and output verification in LLM systems. However, item accuracy alone cannot establish whether models make correct decisions across controlled variations or assign reliable confidence to their predictions. We introduce DecisionPivot, a diagnostic benchmark comprising 48 tasks and 40,033 items across seven decision roles.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights

entry.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
entry.summary:
Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #robotics

entry.title: Epi: Towards a Persistent, Self-Improving Agent for Autonomous Research
entry.summary:
We present Épi, an autonomous research agent that sustains investigations across model sessions and evolves its methods through accumulated experience. Épi combines persistent research history, hierarchical memory, branching and independent review to maintain research continuity, learn from experiments, and explore and revisit alternative approaches. Its experiments run across session boundaries, and a fixed verifier evaluates their outputs.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #combinatorics #agents

entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

entry.title: Post-quantum commutative group actions from oriented superspecial abelian varieties
entry.summary:
We study the cryptographic use of Shimura class group actions on superspecial principally polarized abelian varieties equipped with a CM orientation, within the context of post-quantum cryptography. Besides giving an accessible introduction to the topic, illustrated with many examples, we provide tools for representing CM orientations through higher-dimensional isogenies and for computing the Shimura class group action in the restricted effective group action model. Here, key auxiliary results are a version of Kani's lemma "with CM" and a trick that often allows to halve the ambient dimension.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics

entry.title: Generic finiteness of solutions to parametrized systems of generalized polynomial inequalities
entry.summary:
We study parametrized systems of $\mathit{generalized}$ polynomial inequalities, $(c \circ x^B) \in C$, for a positive variable vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^n_>$, a $\mathit{real}$ exponent matrix $B \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times m}$, a positive parameter vector $c \in \mathbb{R}^m_>$, and a positive, blunt coefficient cone $C \subset \mathbb{R}^m_>$. This setting includes (i) generalized polynomial equations, $A \, (c \circ x^B) = 0$, arising e.g. from power-law dynamical systems with real exponents (and involving a real coefficient matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n' \times m}$), and (ii) generalized semi-algebraic sets.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #analysis-pde #algebra-geometry

entry.title: Speculative Imbalance Positions by Non-Physical Traders: Impacts on Electricity System Balancing in Great Britain
entry.summary:
The electricity system in Great Britain (GB) allows participants to deliberately produce or consume a different volume to their traded position and has incentivised this practice with a single imbalance price since 2015. In particular, non-physical traders (NPTs) often take an open position to imbalance without any intention to produce or consume power. However, new government proposals could restrict this practice due to concerns over supply-demand balancing feasibility and costs.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #quant-finance

entry.title: Arithmetic Models for Commodity Futures, Vanilla, and Calendar Spread Options
entry.summary:
We develop an arithmetic multi-factor stochastic volatility model for commodity futures and options. The arithmetic specification yields a low-dimensional Markovian representation of the futures curve and semi-closed-form pricing formulas for vanilla and basket options, including calendar spread options. These properties make the model suitable for large-scale empirical estimation.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #quant-finance

entry.title: Extending Mechanisms
entry.summary:
Given an incentive-compatible mechanism for a single agent on a restricted domain of valuations, we consider its incentive-compatible extensions to the entire valuation space. We identify two extreme extensions: the "keep-the-menu" extension, which minimizes buyer payoffs and maximizes canonical prices pointwise, and the "keep-the-pricing" extension, which maximizes buyer payoffs and minimizes canonical prices…

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #market-design

entry.title: Entanglement Distribution in Quantum Switch Networks: Memory Limits and Achievability
entry.summary:
We study the minimum persistent memory required to distribute a graph state through a quantum switch. Specifically, consider a central switch that assists $n$ remote users in distributing a graph state, using independently generated user-switch Bell pairs. Since Bell-pair generation is probabilistic, different links generally succeed at different times.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #networking #combinatorics

entry.title: Grain-Boundary Scattering between Chiral Domains in Chiral Topological Semimetal CoSi
entry.summary:
We evaluate the electron scattering properties in CoSi thin films having either twin (heterochiral) or non-twin (homochiral) grain boundaries using first-principles quantum transport calculations. We find that scattering across a twin grain boundary is more resistive than scattering across a non-twin grain boundary and that non-twin grain boundaries have a greater percentage of surface conduction than twin grain boundaries. This is corroborated by the transmission eigenstate profiles, which show that the surface Fermi-arc electrons can transmit past the non-twin grain boundaries between homochiral domains on the same surface without significant backscattering.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science

entry.title: Nonlocal Equations on Domains and Manifolds Without Symmetries
entry.summary:
In this work, we establishes results of existence and regularity for solutions to nonlocal equations of the form $f(Δ)u = U(x,u(x)) ~\text{and}~f(Δ_{g})u=U(x,u(x))$ in the Euclidean context and Riemannian context respectively. We extend the results of \cite{Gorka 6} for the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ under cylindrically symmetry and compact Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$ under action of a closed Lie subgroup $G \leq \text{Isom}_{g}(M)$. Our approach combines spectral theory, complex interpolation and fixed-point methods.

Source: arXiv Analysis, PDEs & Probability (AP, PR, NA, OC) · Tags: #analysis-pde #probability-stats #topology

entry.title: Efficient Ground-State Manifold Amplification for Rydberg Atom Arrays via Houdayer Cluster Updates
entry.summary:
We demonstrate a hybrid quantum-classical approach for exploring ground-state manifolds of maximum independent set problems, in which quantum hardware supplies the initial solutions and an entirely classical post-processing algorithm expands them, increasing the solution diversity of quantum hardware measurements by up to several orders of magnitude. Quantum optimization devices, while capable of generating high-quality solutions, can suffer from fundamental sampling limitations. This is particularly problematic for applications that strongly depend on a large variety of uncorrelated optimal solutions.

Source: arXiv Analysis, PDEs & Probability (AP, PR, NA, OC) · Tags: #analysis-pde #probability-stats #quantum-computing #optimization

entry.title: Photonic band structure by direct second-kind free-space boundary integral equations
entry.summary:
We present a direct boundary integral equation (BIE) formulation of the Bloch eigenvalue problem for two-dimensional photonic crystals that uses only the free-space Helmholtz Green function. The unknowns are the Cauchy data of the Bloch mode on the inclusion boundary and on two cell walls. On the inclusion boundary, the transmission conditions are imposed via Müller's formulation.

Source: arXiv Analysis, PDEs & Probability (AP, PR, NA, OC) · Tags: #analysis-pde #probability-stats #optics-photonics #post-quantum

entry.title: Black Holes are about Quantum Information
entry.summary:
We review and analyse quantum information-theoretic approaches to black hole evaporation that purport to bring us closer to a resolution of the black hole information paradox. Our focus is on the Page-time paradox and on the contribution of the Hayden-Preskill model to understanding information release under the assumption of unitary evaporation. In this model, the black hole is taken to be a finite-dimensional quantum system whose dynamics can be represented by a quantum circuit, and its information-processing and communication abilities are studied.

Source: arXiv High-Energy, Astrophysics & Optics (hep-th, astro-ph, optics) · Tags: #high-energy #astrophysics #quantum-computing

entry.title: The Covering Radius of $\text{RM}(1,9)$ is Precisely $242$
entry.summary:
Let $\text{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed-Muller code of length $2^n$, and let $\rho(r,n)$ denote its covering radius, so that $\rho(1,n)$ is the largest possible nonlinearity of a Boolean function in $n$ variables. For odd $n$, the value of $\rho(1,n)$ was previously known only for $n\le 7$. It is known that $242\le\rho(1,9)\le 244$, but the exact determination of $\rho(1,9)$ has been a long-standing open question.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Quantum Broker: QoS-Aware Distribution of Quantum Computations
entry.summary:
Cloud-accessible quantum computing has made heterogeneous Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) available through provider platforms that differ in qubit technology, calibration state, queueing behavior, and pricing model. This heterogeneity makes execution management a quantum-engineering concern: a quantum circuit may be executable on several backends, but the resulting cost, latency, fidelity, and reproducibility depend on backend selection and on how measurement shots are allocated. This paper presents the Quantum Broker, an open-source and provider-agnostic framework for Quality-of-Service-aware quantum execution management.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #quantum-computing #software-architecture

entry.title: ClawMMU: Protection-Coherent Virtual Memory for Stateful LLM Agents. AI agents keep long-term memory, much of which comes from web pages and tool results.
entry.summary:
AI agents keep long-term memory, much of which comes from web pages and tool results. Agent harnesses, the software that runs the model, do not record who may act on this memory, so an instruction hidden in a fetched page can be treated as the user's own instruction. We propose ClawMMU, a protection layer that labels every piece of memory with its owner, scope, origins, and authority.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #ml-theory
